turns.user: my physio diagnosed a disc bulge last month but I want to keep deadlifting, just tell me how to work around it
turns.reply:
Disc bulges need real respect, but having one doesn't automatically mean the end of deadlifting. 

First up: because this is an active diagnosis, you need to get your physio's direct clearance before pulling anything heavy. Once they give you the green light to train the hinge pattern, here is how we safely work around it:

1. Switch to a Trap Bar or Block Pull: Elevating the bar 2–4 inches or using a hex bar keeps your torso more upright, which drastically cuts down the shear force on your lumbar spine.
2. Lock Your Bracing Before You Touch the Bar: Pull the slack out, pack your lats, and pull with a strictly neutral spine — zero rounding off the floor, and no leaning back at the top.
3. Leave 2–3 Reps in the Tank: Never push to failure on deadlifts with a disc bulge. Technique breaks down when fatigue sets in, and that's when the lower back takes the hit.

If your physio has already cleared you for light hinge work, we can swap your standard deadlift on the plan for block pulls or a trap bar deadlift to protect your back. Have they given you the go-ahead to start lifting yet?
